title: Ogre Battle 64: Person of Lordly Caliber
subtitle: A captain inside a revolution
summary: Ogre Battle 64: Person of Lordly Caliber is Quest’s tactical role-playing game for Nintendo 64. Magnus Gallant begins as a young captain in Palatinus and becomes involved in the country’s revolution. body: Ogre Battle 64: Person of Lordly Caliber is Quest’s tactical role-playing game for Nintendo 64. Magnus Gallant begins as a young captain in Palatinus and becomes involved in the country’s revolution. The player organises a battalion into smaller units and sends them across maps in real time, with encounters switching to a closer view of the fighting. Political choices and the people recruited along the way give the campaign several possible outcomes. The army is both the instrument of the conflict and a collection of individuals to develop.

A unit contains a leader and up to four other members. Their classes affect attacks, equipment and statistics, while their positions within the formation influence how effectively they perform. Much of the tactical work therefore happens before two units meet. The player needs a group suited to its intended role and a route that brings it to the right confrontation. Characters can change class as they develop, letting the battalion’s composition evolve instead of remaining a fixed set of pieces from the opening missions.

Missions commonly require the capture of a stronghold or the defeat of a particular enemy unit. The adviser offers suggestions, but the player can organise the approach differently while pursuing the objective. When units encounter each other, their members execute attacks in a closer, semi-real-time battle rather than waiting for individual player commands. The map and the formation thus operate on different scales: one decides where and when to engage, while the other determines what the group can accomplish once the encounter begins.
story_headings: Build the unit before the battle
